LRCX.thesis_one_line: Excellent wafer-fab-equipment franchise with record margins, but priced for growth roughly triple its own 10-year history.
kill_criteria: Reported revenue growth decelerates below 15% YoY for two consecutive quarters
China revenue share stabilises or reverses its decline and Taiwan/Korea demand fails to keep offsetting it, evidenced by a guidance cut
Non-GAAP gross margin falls back below 48% for a full quarter
Book-to-bill (or qualitative order commentary) turns negative for two consecutive quarters
The MATCH Act or a further export-control tightening is enacted with a disclosed revenue impact beyond the ~$600M/year headwind already guided
key_adverse_facts: V1's own reverse DCF requires 48.5%/yr FCFF growth for 10 years vs a historical 5-year CAGR of only 9.7%/yr and 10-year CAGR of 14.7%/yr
NTM P/E of 31.4x sits at the 80th percentile of its own 177-month trading history -- one of the more expensive points in its own history, not a discount

China revenue mix fell from 43% to 26% of sales in three quarters under export controls; a homegrown Chinese DUV lithography competitor has begun shipments (5 units 2026, 20 planned 2027) and the pending US MATCH Act would tighten export controls further
Forward guidance (Sept 2026 quarter) implies a +20.5% sequential revenue jump, the largest in the two-year data window, raising the bar for the very next print
FQ4 FY26 GAAP figures were not independently verified from the 10-K in the time available; the quoted 52.0% gross margin / 38.4% operating margin / $1.82 EPS are non-GAAP company-reported figures
data_conflicts: Triage advanced LRCX citing a 'net-cash-implied required growth of ~8%', but V1's actual reverse-DCF (FCFF at 11.8% WACC over 10 years fading to 3% terminal) implies 48.5%/yr -- the triage appears to have used an easier heuristic than the systematic model's own framework; this dossier sides with V1's harder test
LRCX.confidence_in_thesis: medium (guidance-vs-actual track record and China-mix trend are filing/press verified; FQ4 FY26 GAAP detail and FQ1/FQ2 FY26 guidance-vs-actual could not be independently confirmed in the time available)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's base case (20.3% growth, 20.4x exit multiple) implies a -20.2%/yr 3-year return and its own street-flag notes the base case is below the Street's 12-month low target; this dossier agrees the 48.5%/yr implied 10-year growth is well above any defensible base case (my own base case ~high-teens-to-low-20s%/yr) and confirms the read with the sector-appropriate cross-check that a 31.4x NTM P/E at the 80th percentile of 14.75 years of history is not a value discount.

MPWR.thesis_one_line: Power-chip supplier riding real AI data-center demand, but priced for a decade of fast growth while a securities-fraud suit over its top customer and an unremediated accounting weakness remain unresolved.
kill_criteria: Any quarter where YoY revenue growth decelerates below 30%, roughly two-thirds of the current run-rate
An adverse ruling, settlement disclosure, or SEC enforcement action in the Waterford Twp. securities action or the Miller derivative suit that confirms material, un-remediated disclosure failures
The material weakness remains unremediated for two more consecutive 10-K/10-Q filings without a disclosed remediation timeline
Nvidia (or the single largest disclosed AI-platform customer) is confirmed, via a 10-K customer-concentration disclosure or company statement, to have reduced or in-sourced power-delivery content
Gross margin falls below 53% (below the two-year band of 55.1-55.4%) for a full quarter
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 10-K discloses a restatement (Audit Committee determination 2026-02-26): the FY2024 10-K and all 2025 10-Qs 'should no longer be relied upon' due to an unintentional deferred-income-tax accounting error tied to a foreign tax incentive, cutting FY2024 income-tax benefit/net deferred taxes by $194.6 million; the resulting material weakness is not yet remediated

Securities class action Waterford Twp. Gen. Emps. Ret. Sys. v. Monolithic Power Systems, Inc., et al. (No. 25-cv-220, W.D. Wash., filed 2026-02-04) alleges the company hid critical Nvidia power-module defects and order cancellations; motion to dismiss largely denied 2026-05-07, rejecting a fraud-by-hindsight defence; consolidated derivative suit Miller v. Hsing, et al. (No. 25-cv-527) proceeds alongside it

Q4 2024 GAAP diluted EPS of $25.71 (restated) versus a $2.79-3.71/quarter run-rate every other quarter is almost entirely a one-off tax benefit, not operating performance -- a major GAAP earnings-quality distortion if not separated from the trend

b1 quant composite ranks MPWR in the bottom quintile of the ~500-name coverage universe (decile 2, live_rank 445), driven by weak value metrics (ep, fcfp, bp all near the bottom) and a low earnings-surprise score (SUE 0.196) despite large headline growth
Trailing GAAP P/E of roughly 83x on TTM EPS of ~$16.43; independent reverse DCF implies ~31.6%/yr FCFF growth for 10 years versus a 2-year historical revenue CAGR of 23.8%/yr
data_conflicts: Triage advanced MPWR on '+48% revenue growth and +112% EPS growth against a 42x NTM P/E' (sub-1 PEG optics), but b1's systematic quant score ranks it in the bottom quintile of the entire coverage universe on quality and value; this dossier sides with the quant model's scepticism given the SUE of only 0.196 (the growth was not a surprise relative to the stock's own volatility, i.e. already priced in)
MPWR.confidence_in_thesis: medium (restatement, litigation status and quarterly XBRL figures are primary-sourced; Q3/Q4 2025 figures were derived by subtraction from annual totals rather than filed directly, next-earnings date and some guidance-vs-actual history are estimated/incomplete)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: MPWR has no row in v1_valuation_table.csv or v1_valuation.json (v1_verdict null). This dossier built an independent reverse DCF (same FCFF-with-3%-terminal-fade structure as V1, WACC ~10.3% since MPWR carries no funded debt): implied 10-year growth ~31.6%/yr versus a 2-year historical revenue CAGR of 23.8%/yr and this analyst's own base case of ~20-24%/yr -- implied growth is above the base case, consistent with an 'expensive' dossier view even without a V1 row to reconcile against.

MU.thesis_one_line: The best memory franchise in the world, mid a real AI/HBM pricing supercycle, but priced for that supercycle to keep escalating for a decade -- a bet memory has never delivered.
kill_criteria: Sequential DRAM/HBM ASP declines for two consecutive quarters, first visible via gross margin compression from the 84-86% FQ3/FQ4 FY26 level
GAAP gross margin falls below 65% for a full quarter, roughly the FQ1 FY26 level
Capex guidance is cut versus the ~$10B/quarter FQ4 FY26 run-rate while HBM demand commentary stays positive
Net cash position turns to net debt, or buybacks are suspended while capex stays elevated
The DRAM price-fixing class action (N.D. Cal., filed 2026-06-25) results in an adverse ruling, DOJ referral, or negotiated output/pricing remedy
key_adverse_facts: A federal class action filed 2026-06-25 alleges Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix conspired to restrict DRAM supply and inflate prices, citing a 700% price surge over four years -- directly relevant because this dossier's entire bull case rests on the pricing the suit says is manipulated; Scott+Scott is separately investigating officers/directors for related fiduciary-duty claims
V1's own base case (16.8% growth assumption) implies a -36.8%/yr 3-year return, and its street-flag notes the base case is below even the Street's own 12-month low price target ($361 vs $1,082 spot)

P/B of approximately 12.1x (equity $100.7B / ~1.129B shares = ~$89.2 book value/share) is rich even against past memory-cycle peaks on the sector's own preferred valuation lens (P/B through the cycle, since trailing P/E is structurally inverted for memory)

A U.S. International Trade Commission investigation was instituted involving Micron in 2026; complainant/respondent status and product scope were not independently confirmed in the time available for this pass

FQ4 FY26 guidance ($50B revenue, ~86% gross margin, $31 EPS) implies a fourth consecutive quarter of an outsized beat-and-raise, reported just 5 days after this dossier's price cutoff (earnings 2026-09-30)
data_conflicts: V1 itself flags: 'D3 TTM revenue implies an implausible EBIT margin (65.6%)'. This dossier independently confirms 65.6% is the correct blended TTM figure (TTM EBIT $59.2B / TTM revenue $90.3B) given the mid-year pricing spike -- not a data error, but a genuine, extreme, filing-verified margin level that is itself the valuation risk
MU.confidence_in_thesis: high (revenue/margin/EPS figures and guidance-vs-actual for the last 3 releases are directly filing- and press-release-verified; only the ITC investigation's scope is unconfirmed)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1 labels MU 'fair' (score 0.162, driven mainly by a cheap-screening 22nd-percentile NTM P/E of 6.79x), but V1's own reverse DCF requires 33.0%/yr FCFF growth for 10 years -- above MU's trailing 5-year delivered CAGR (28.8%) -- and its own base case returns -36.8%/yr over 3 years. This dossier disagrees with the 'fair' label: per the sector playbook, a single-digit P/E on record memory earnings is a warning, not a value signal, and the P/B cross-check (~12.1x) confirms a full, not discounted, price. Dossier view is 'expensive', i.e. implied growth is above this analyst's own base case (~18-22%/yr) -- inconsistent with V1's labelled verdict even though the two analyses' quantitative growth figures (33.0% implied vs history) point the same direction.
